prerequisites: Students must have completed a general course on materials science in the undergraduate degree prior to the Master's.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to distinguish different types of corrosion, oxidation, wear or other types of degradation.
Ability to evaluate the resistance of materials against corrosive actions at low and high temperature and to make decisions for their protection against these types of actions.

Ability to manage and use the different testing techniques employed to evaluate oxidation/corrosion resistance, to perform the corresponding measurements and to interpret the results obtained in these tests.
Ability to apply design criteria, material selection, and coatings oriented to the prevention of corrosion and material degradation.
Understand the basic fundamentals of corrosion and material degradation processes.
Know the classification of the different forms of degradation based on the process or processes affecting each of them.
Understand the different means of protection against various types of degradation.
Know the different surface treatments and coatings available in the market to protect against corrosion and degradation processes.
Know the different degradation processes of coatings.
Know the measures to apply to mitigate degradation processes.
Identify the different processes of corrosion, wear, or other types of degradation in materials subjected to these situations.
Select materials, treatments, and/or coatings in order to produce novel products or products with better performance against situations of corrosion, wear, or other types of degradation.
Manage technical specifications and available regulations on materials and coatings, their analysis, and corrosion and wear tests.
Acquisition of skills, work systematic, and handling of available laboratory equipment to perform corrosion tests.
Combine acquired knowledge to obtain detailed information on degradation processes under study and solve practical problems that may arise.
Encourage in the student an interest in acquiring practical knowledge.
Lay the groundwork for the student to be able to apply the acquired knowledge in engineering.
Formation of an open, critical, cooperative, and entrepreneurial spirit.

syllabus_topics: General aspects of corrosion. Electrochemical corrosion. Galvanic cells. Kinetics of aqueous corrosion. Oxidation of metals. Measurement of corrosion and oxidation rates.

Degradation of metals: Macroscopic corrosion. Aqueous corrosion. Atmospheric corrosion. Galvanic corrosion. High-temperature gaseous corrosion. Pitting corrosion. Crevice corrosion. Filiform corrosion. Molten salt corrosion. Molten metal corrosion.
Degradation of metals: Embrittlement. Molten metal induced embrittlement. Solid material induced embrittlement. Irradiation embrittlement. Thermal embrittlement. Hydrogen embrittlement.
Degradation of metals: Wear and assisted corrosion. Types of wear. Corrosion-wear. Erosion-corrosion. Stress corrosion cracking. Corrosion-fatigue. Microbiologically influenced corrosion.
Corrosion testing and evaluation. Electrochemical corrosion testing methods. Corrosion chamber tests. In-service simulation tests. Corrosion evaluation.
Polymer degradation. Classification of polymers, structure and properties. Chemical attack degradation. Thermal degradation. Radiation degradation. Ultraviolet degradation. Biodegradation.
Protective Coatings. Types of coatings. Surface preparation and coating application. Selection of the appropriate coating.
Degradation of Coatings. Description and detection of degradation mechanisms. Susceptibility to coating degradation. Mitigation of coating degradation.
Other methods of corrosion protection. Cathodic protection. Anodic protection. Corrosion inhibitors.
Designing to control and prevent corrosion.

assessment_methods.method: Evaluation of work performed during practical classes (exercises, questionnaires and laboratory practices)
Group work and presentation/discussion in class
Written test (questionnaire) on the complete course content

assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of 40% from practical class work, 20% from group work and presentation, and 40% from a final written test. A minimum of 4 points out of 10 is required in the final written evaluation to pass the subject.
